text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL DEFICIT WORRIES IMF, BUT ECONOMY GROWS

The Brazilian economy showed stronger growth in 1996, while inflation fell to 9 percent at year's end. But a wider current account deficit in the balance of payments and a weaker fiscal picture imply risks, said IMF's World Economic Outlook.
-- CREDIT GROWS SLIGHTLY, SAYS CENTRAL BANK

Bank loans to individuals and companies rose only 1.9 percent to 79.5 billion reais from 78.1 billion reais between March 1 and March 20, says an internal report by Brazil's Central Bank mistakenly distributed to the press Wednesday. The slight expansion suggests eventual credit restrictions would be unnecessary.
-- CVRD'S SALE FACES A NEW OBSTACLE

The vice-president of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), Jose Pio Borges, who heads the privatization plan of state miner Companhia Vale do Rio Doce, is an active member of Aracruz Celulose's Board of Directors. This could create conflict-of-interest problems.
Aracruz's main shareholders include two members of one consortium interested in CVRD: Anglo American and Banco Safra.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- GOVERNMENT SUFFERS REFORM AMENDMENT DEFEAT
The Brazilian government suffered its first defeat in the Chamber of Deputies when it failed to muster enough votes to add an amendment to its civil service reform bill.
-- SENATE APPROVES RESTRICTIONS ON PRESIDENTIAL DECREES

Brazil's Senate approved a bill that would change rules governing the use of presidential decrees in an initial round of voting. The new law would extend the validity of a presidential decree to 90 days from the current 30, but it would allow the government to renew it for only one extra period of 90 days.
O GLOBO
-- INDIANS HOLD HOSTAGE TO CLAIM LAND

Pataxo indians held Brazil's National Indian Foundation (Funai) president Julio Geiger hostage and invaded five farms bordered on their reserves in the northeastern state of Bahia to press demands for land.
-- SUPREME COURT MAINTAINS CVRD'S SALE BY REJECTING ACTION

Brazil's Supreme Court gave a key victory to the government and its plans to privatize state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce by rejecting a court case brought by the Order of Brazilian Lawyers (OAB). The case alleged the privatization program was unconstitutional.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-2485412))
